answer_1.quote: We introduce INQUISITIVE, a new, large-scale dataset of questions ... We further present question generation models on this data using GPT-2, a state-of-the-art pre-trained language model often used in natural language generation tasks.

answer_2.quote: We also use several metrics that capture the generation behavior of the models. These include: (1) Measuring the extent of copying. Train-n: percentage of n-grams in the generated questions that also appeared in some question in the training set. (2) Article-n: percentage of n-grams in the generated questions that also appeared in either the sentence where the question is asked, or any prior sentence in the same article. (3) Span: percentage of words appeared in the annotated span that also appeared in the generated question.

answer_4.quote: We mainly perform human evaluation on the generated questions by collecting the same validity judgments from Mechanical Turk as described in Section 3.3.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators judged each generated question for validity, whether it is related to the highlighted span, and whether it is already answered in the prior context.
